newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark may buy own shares from state.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark may buy own shares from state.

text.p: Partly-privatised Danish Telecoms group Tele Danmark could buy its own shares when the government sells off more of its 52 percent stake, managing director Hans Wuertzen said on Thursday.
Wuertzen welcomed Wednesday's government announcement that the state would sell all or part of its remaining holding sometime after this autumn.

"Tele Danmark sees as positive the the state's decision on a share sale. It is a natural extension of the deregulation of the (Danish) telecommunications industry and matches international developments," he said in a statement.
He said that the stock market looked generally positive and the prospects of selling the shares was good, irrespective of the size of the offer, which he said would be in 1998.
Based on current prices the state's holding was worth at least 23 billion crowns he added.

"There is a possibility that Tele Danmark itself will buy part of the shares and that is being considered," he said, adding that such a purchase would reduce the group's own capital while a sale on the open market would not.
The Danish telecommunications industry was deregulated last year and several foreign competitors are building up a local presence, among them Sweden's Telia and France Telecom

Recent market talk said that British Telecommunications was eyeing a stake in Tele Danmark but the Danish group on June 6 said it had heard nothing from B.T. and Wuertzen's statement made no reference to the idea.
The share closed in Copenhagen on Thursday at 344.00 crowns, one crown up on Wednesday.
